ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 30^\circ$, point $P$ is located inside $\angle AOB$ with $OP = 3$. Points $M$ and $N$ are moving points on the rays $OA$ and $OB$, respectively. What is the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ when its perimeter is at its minimum?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct the symmetric points $E$ and $D$ of point $P$ with respect to $OA$ and $OB$, respectively, and connect $DN$, $EM$, $DE$, $OD$, $OE$,\\
then $OA$ perpendicularly bisects $PE$ and $OB$ perpendicularly bisects $PD$,\\
$\therefore EM=PM$, $DN=PN$, $OD=OP=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $PM+MN+PN=EM+MN+DN$,\\
Knowing that the length of the segment between two points is the shortest, when points $E$, $M$, $N$, $D$ are collinear, the value of $EM+MN+DN$ is minimal, and the minimum value is equal to the length of $DE$,\\
$\because OE=OP$, $OA\perp PE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOE=\angle AOP$ (the three lines of an isosceles triangle coincide),\\
Similarly, it can be derived: $\angle BOD=\angle BOP$,\\
$\because \angle AOB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOP+\angle AOP=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOE=\angle BOD+\angle BOP+\angle AOP+\angle AOE=2\left(\angle BOP+\angle AOP\right)=60^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because OD=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DOE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore DE=OD=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of $EM+MN+DN$ is 3,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $\boxed{3}$,\\

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a 30-degree angle with vertex O, lower ray OA containing M, upper ray OB containing N, and P inside the angle; the perimeter is the broken path P-M-N-P. Reflect P across OA to a point E and across OB to a point D. Since M lies on OA and N lies on OB, reflection gives PM = EM and PN = DN, so the perimeter equals EM + MN + ND. By the triangle inequality, EM + MN + ND is at least ED, with equality when E, M, N, D are collinear. Compute ED: reflection preserves OP, so OE = OD = OP = 3. If angle AOP = alpha and angle POB = beta, then alpha + beta = 30 degrees, and the angle EOD equals 2(alpha + beta) = 60 degrees. Hence triangle EOD has two sides 3 with included angle 60 degrees, so it is equilateral and ED = 3. Therefore the minimum perimeter is 3.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a variable broken path from P to M on the lower ray OA, then to N on the upper ray OB, and back to P. Treat the minimizing path as an optical/billiard path reflecting off the two rays. At an interior minimum, the path must satisfy the equal-angle reflection condition at M with respect to OA and at N with respect to OB; this can be justified either by a small-variation argument along each ray or by differentiating the perimeter with M and N constrained to their rays. Now unfold the two reflections: replace the segment PM by the segment from the mirror image of P across OA, and replace PN by the segment to the mirror image of P across OB. The equal-angle condition means the unfolded path is one straight line, so the minimum perimeter is the distance between those two mirror images. To compute that distance, put P at polar angle alpha inside the 30-degree angle. Its reflection across OA has polar angle -alpha; its reflection across OB has polar angle 60 degrees - alpha. These two mirror images are both distance 3 from O and differ in direction by 60 degrees, so their distance is 3. Thus the minimum perimeter is 3.

推理：把周长 PM+MN+NP 看成从 P 到 M，再到 N，再回到 P 的折线路径，其中 M、N 分别被限制在两条射线上。按光路反射思想，若周长取得内部最小值，则在 M 处关于 OA 满足等角反射，在 N 处关于 OB 满足等角反射。

将路径展开：设 E 是 P 关于 OA 的对称点，D 是 P 关于 OB 的对称点。由于反射对称，PM=EM，PN=DN，所以三角形周长
PM+MN+PN=EM+MN+DN。
当 E、M、N、D 共线时，折线 EM+MN+ND 最短，最小值等于直线段 ED 的长度。

计算 ED：设 P 在角 AOB 内的极角为 α，其中 0<α<30°，且 OP=3。P 关于 OA 反射后，E 的极角为 -α；P 关于 OB 反射后，D 的极角为 2·30°-α=60°-α。于是 OE=OD=OP=3，且 E、D 的方向角相差
(60°-α)-(-α)=60°。
所以三角形 OED 中 OE=OD=3，夹角 ∠EOD=60°，因此 △OED 为等边三角形，ED=3。

因此三角形 PMN 周长的最小值为 3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 30^\circ$, point $P$ is located inside $\angle AOB$ with $OP = 3$. Points $M$ and $N$ are moving points on the rays $OA$ and $OB$, respectively. What is the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ when its perimeter is at its minimum?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct the symmetric points $E$ and $D$ of point $P$ with respect to $OA$ and $OB$, respectively, and connect $DN$, $EM$, $DE$, $OD$, $OE$,\\
then $OA$ perpendicularly bisects $PE$ and $OB$ perpendicularly bisects $PD$,\\
$\therefore EM=PM$, $DN=PN$, $OD=OP=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $PM+MN+PN=EM+MN+DN$,\\
Knowing that the length of the segment between two points is the shortest, when points $E$, $M$, $N$, $D$ are collinear, the value of $EM+MN+DN$ is minimal, and the minimum value is equal to the length of $DE$,\\
$\because OE=OP$, $OA\perp PE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOE=\angle AOP$ (the three lines of an isosceles triangle coincide),\\
Similarly, it can be derived: $\angle BOD=\angle BOP$,\\
$\because \angle AOB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOP+\angle AOP=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOE=\angle BOD+\angle BOP+\angle AOP+\angle AOE=2\left(\angle BOP+\angle AOP\right)=60^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because OD=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DOE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore DE=OD=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of $EM+MN+DN$ is 3,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $\boxed{3}$,\\
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an angle AOB with O as the vertex, OA is the lower ray, OB is the upper oblique ray, and point P is inside angle AOB; point M is located on ray OA, point N is located on ray OB, and triangle PMN is drawn. The problem gives ∠AOB = 30°, OP = 3. Reasoning: According to the method, construct point E as the reflection of point P about OA, and point D as the reflection about OB. Because M is on OA and N is on OB, after reflection PM = EM, PN = DN. Therefore the perimeter of triangle PMN, PM + MN + PN = EM + MN + DN. By the fact that the line segment between two points is the shortest, the length of the broken-line path E-M-N-D is at least ED; when E, M, N, D are collinear, the minimum value is attained, so the minimum perimeter equals ED. Let ∠AOP = α, ∠POB = β, then α + β = 30°. Reflection makes ∠AOE = ∠AOP = α, ∠BOD = ∠BOP = β, so ∠EOD = 2(α + β) = 60°. Also OE = OP = OD = 3, therefore triangle EOD has two sides equal to 3 and included angle 60°, so it is an equilateral triangle, hence ED = 3. Thus the minimum perimeter is 3.
